clue.text: Tatum set out to accompany one such performer

parts.note: Art Tatum was the great American jazz pianist, so his first name is supplied
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: set out suggests things laid out afresh, so the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets off to play alongside a jazz pianist like Art Tatum.
explanation.walkthrough: Art Tatum, the American jazz pianist, supplies his first name; 'such' links to the definition, Tatum himself being a fine example of the type.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer, a synonym for a stage performer.

clue.text: It's fit to retrieve information from

definitions.meaning: a sudden fit or outburst, as of rage
to ... a file or database is to get data out of it

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a sudden attack of feeling and a verb for reading data.

clue.text: Heavyweight with a posh car cover

parts.note: a tonne is a metric heavy weight of 1000 kilograms
U is the abbreviation for upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A big man has a cover for a smart motor car.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonneau cover is the flexible cover over the open rear part of an open car or pickup.

clue.text: Bright spark, one given books in plant

indicators.note: the one and books are put in the plant, so they go inside its name

parts.note: scilla is a genus of bulbous plants, the squills
I is the Roman numeral for one
NT stands for the New Testament, the books of the Bible after the Old

explanation.surface: A clever child is given some books to read in a greenhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bright spark' suggests a clever person, but it is the definition read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Scintilla is Latin for a spark, now used for a tiny glimmer or trace.

clue.text: Circle, not line, represents such a charmer

definitions.text: Circle, not line, represents such a charmer

parts.words: Circle, not line, represents such a charmer
parts.note: remove L for line from the word circle to get the name of the sorceress in the Odyssey, an example of this kind of charmer

explanation.surface: A ring rather than a straight line symbolises a seductive woman.
explanation.walkthrough: CIRCLE without L gives CIRCE, who turned Odysseus's men into pigs; she is the example the clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchantress is a woman who casts spells or captivates, a charmer by magic or allure.

clue.text: Funny, finding isinglass in lowest part of ridge

indicators.note: the isinglass is found in, so placed within, the low point of the ridge

parts.note: a col is the lowest point on a mountain ridge, a pass
mica is also called isinglass, the thin transparent mineral sheets

explanation.surface: A hiker comes across something odd: a mineral in the pass between peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comical is amusing, a straightforward synonym for funny.

clue.text: One swimming in sea for a joke

definitions.meaning: ... as a noun or verb means a hoax or a leg-pull, as in codswallop

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a common North Atlantic fish and also, informally, a hoax or jest.

clue.text: Stingy type we may find boring

definitions.meaning: a ... hoards money and hates spending it
a large auger for boring wells

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a skinflint and the name of a well-boring drill.

clue.text: Idiot having pork pie with tea

parts.note: char is British slang for tea, from Chinese cha
pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie, often shortened to porky

explanation.surface: A fool is having a pork pie and a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is British slang for a fool, as in 'a right Charlie'.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlie is a silly person, a British colloquial term for an idiot.

clue.text: Business graduate's surprised cry about part of Italy

indicators.note: the cry goes about, around, the graduate

parts.note: lordy is an exclamation of surprise
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration graduate

explanation.surface: A new business graduate exclaims in surprise on arriving in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lombardy is a region of northern Italy, with Milan as its capital.

clue.text: Certain French wine formerly consumed among diplomats

indicators.note: the whole assembly sits among the diplomats, so inside their abbreviation

parts.note: CD stands for Corps Diplomatique, the diplomatic corps

indicators.note: the wine is consumed, swallowed, by the word for formerly, so it goes inside it

parts.note: once means formerly, at some time in the past
vin is the French word for wine

explanation.surface: Embassy staff are sure they once drank French wine at a reception.
explanation.definitionFit: To be convinced is to be certain or sure of something, a synonym.

clue.text: Direction dangerous for some setting up colony

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south, a compass direction
warm can mean hazardous or hostile, as in warm work or making things warm for someone

explanation.surface: A warning that heading a certain way is perilous for some people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for some' qualifies the uncommon sense of warm as dangerous, and links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees swarm when a queen leaves with part of the hive to found a new colony.

clue.text: It may make us take shelter in centre of Boston

definitions.text: It may make us take shelter in centre of Boston

indicators.note: the shelter sits in the centre of the city's name, so it is put inside
the centre of a six-letter word is its two middle letters

parts.note: lee is shelter from wind, the sheltered side

explanation.surface: Bad weather in downtown Boston sends people running for cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy driving rain is the sort of weather that forces people indoors for cover.

clue.text: American paintings put back, inter alia, down under

indicators.note: to inter is to bury, so these letters are buried inside the word alia

parts.note: US is short for American, of the United States

indicators.note: put back signals that the word for paintings is written in reverse

parts.note: art means paintings collectively

explanation.surface: Among other things, American paintings are returned from down under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inter alia' reads as Latin for 'among other things', but 'inter' is the burying verb and the Latin word is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Down under is the informal name for Australia and New Zealand, seen from the northern hemisphere.

clue.text: Building materials need taking to task: a fine firm's first to be called in

indicators.note: the short pieces are called in, brought inside the telling-off

parts.note: scolding is taking someone to task, telling them off
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word firm's

explanation.surface: A building firm needs a telling-off and a fine, and the boss is summoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaffolding is the framework of poles and planks used as a temporary structure on buildings.

clue.text: Complete second side a top teacher assembled at maximum speed

parts.note: full means complete, entire
S is the abbreviation for second, as in time
a side is a team in sport
the head is the headteacher, the top teacher in a school

explanation.surface: A school sports side and its head assemble in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Full steam ahead is the idiom for going as fast as possible, from steam engines.

clue.text: An Alsatian night worker, one receiving regular payments

parts.note: nuit is French for night, spoken in Alsace
an ant is a worker, from the worker ants of a colony

explanation.surface: A German shepherd dog works through the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alsatian' suggests the dog but means from Alsace, a French region, so the French word is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuitant is a person who receives an annuity, a fixed yearly sum.

clue.text: Knitted jacket for a corgi

definitions.meaning: one of the two breeds of Welsh corgi

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a knitted woollen jacket and a breed of Welsh corgi.

clue.text: Very fast, as some waders move?

definitions.text: Very fast, as some waders move?

parts.words: Very fast, as some waders move?
parts.note: a phrase for great speed, read literally as the gait of the knot, a wading shore bird, also a unit of speed at sea

explanation.surface: Wading birds dash along a beach at great speed.
explanation.walkthrough: The knot is a sandpiper-like wading bird, so the speed idiom doubles as a description of a flock of them moving.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very fast, the knot being a nautical speed unit.

clue.text: As nice as river can be, in parts

indicators.note: can be suggests these letters may be made into something else, so they are rearranged

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A river can be just as pleasant in some places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' at the start looks like a comparison, but it is the chemical symbol, the definition. 'can be' rearranges NICE, AS and R; 'in parts' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic, element number 33.

clue.text: Fairy queen who sleeps there some time of the night?

definitions.text: Fairy queen who sleeps there some time of the night?

parts.words: Fairy queen who sleeps there some time of the night?
parts.note: the fairy queen in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, who sleeps in a bower in the wood for part of the night

explanation.surface: A fairy queen sleeps out in the wood for part of the night.
explanation.walkthrough: In A Midsummer Night's Dream, the queen of the fairies sleeps in her bower in the wood, where Oberon anoints her eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is queen of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Bone found by mate? Half a dozen, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: cock is British slang for a mate, as in 'all right, cock?'; half a dozen is six

explanation.surface: A dog finds a bone near its pal, apparently about six of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The coccyx is the small tailbone at the base of the spine.

clue.text: Girl's met by another breaking up

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, here with its possessive s
per means by, as in per annum
Sal is another girl's name, short for Sally or Sarah

explanation.surface: One girl meets another and their friendship falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Dispersal is a scattering or breaking up of a crowd, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Upshot of historic victory in county king abandoned

indicators.note: the victory goes in the shortened county name, so inside it
the king is abandoned, so his letter is dropped from the county

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess
VE is Victory in Europe, the 1945 Allied victory

explanation.surface: The result of a famous victory celebrated in a county without its king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'historic victory' points to 1945's VE Day, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An event can mean an outcome or result, as in 'in the event', a synonym for upshot.

clue.text: Short prelude certain troubadours pen

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Some wandering minstrels write a brief opening piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' reads as 'write', but it means enclose: the answer is held in certaIN TROubadours.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the abbreviated form of introduction, a short opening passage.

clue.text: Magical being, one with the light brown hair, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.words: one with the light brown hair
parts.note: Jeannie is the girl in Stephen Foster's song Jeanie with the Light Brown Hair

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale creature is pictured as a fair-haired girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie is a spirit from Arabian tales, a magical being granting wishes.

clue.text: Like our monarchs cooking crab in tin

indicators.note: cooking the crab mixes up the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Royal cooks preparing crab in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Britannic means British, as in Her Britannic Majesty, the style of British monarchs.

clue.text: Run past end of lake

parts.note: by means past, as in to walk by

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word lake

explanation.surface: A jogger runs past the far end of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored when the ball passes the batsman without being hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bye is a run scored from a ball that passes the batsman, a cricket term.

clue.text: Americans wear one to canoodle before match

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle, canoodle
a tie is a sporting match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A couple have a cuddle before going to the football.
explanation.definitionFit: Necktie is the American term for a tie, the strip of cloth worn round the collar.

clue.text: Cakes spectators brought to the French

parts.note: the gate is the number of spectators at a sports match
aux is French for to the, before a plural noun

explanation.surface: Fans are treated to French pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: GATE is British for the attendance at a football match.
explanation.definitionFit: Gateaux are rich layered cream cakes, the plural of the French word for cake.
